Article Title: Police were helpless, people feared mafia before 2017: UP CM Yogi

NEW DELHI: Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath on Thursday said that before BJP came into the power in the year 2017, people of UP were disturbed and troubled by the influence of mafia and the police were unable to help the people of the state because they were helpless.The state has experienced a lot of challenges on every front, CM Yogi stated this while attending a flag off ceremony of 87 Interceptor Vehicles equipped with advanced equipment."It was the most populous state yet lagged in the economy, recruitment, the adoption of emerging technologies, and the implementation of welfare schemes. Article Title: 'Indomitable bravery’: Indian Flydubai pilot Smit Machchhar to be awarded ‘Visisht Gujarat Garima Award’
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: The Gujarat government on Thursday announced that they will award Indian pilot Smit Machchhar with the 'Visisht Gujarat Garima Award' for fighting his copilot who allegedly planned to crash the plane that was flying from Dubai to Tel Aviv.Captain Smit Machchhar was stabbed by his Omani co-pilot while fighting him in the cockpit, but fought back and was severely injured. The plane made an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia with all the passengers safe."The courage of Captain Smit Machchhar, the pilot of the flight headed to Israel, is being saluted by the entire world today. Despite being drenched in blood due to the attack, he displayed indomitable bravery to save the lives of 174 passengers—a feat that is profoundly inspiring and commendable," said Gujarat CM Bhupendra Patel on X."This valiant son of Gujarat has illuminated the name of Gujarat and the nation across the globe through his heroism. The Gujarati spirit flowing in his veins fills us all with immense pride. To honor his extraordinary act of bravery and humanity, the Government of Gujarat will bestow upon Captain Smit Machhar the 'Visisht Gujarat Garima Award'," he added.Further praying for his swift recovery, the CM said, "The empathy and prayers of the nation's citizens are with Captain Smit Machchhar."Captain Smit Machchhar has been hailed for his courage after being stabbed by his Omani co-pilot during the Dubai-Tel Aviv flight, with Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and US President Donald Trump among those praising his actions. PM Modi said Machchhar had shown “remarkable patience, presence of mind, and courage” and described him as a “HERO”, saying his valour helped save hundreds of lives and avert a major tragedy.Netanyahu also saluted Machchhar for his “extraordinary bravery”, saying that despite being stabbed and seriously injured, he fought back, opened the cockpit door and enabled passengers and crew to overpower the attacker. Trump similarly called the Indian pilot “a hero”, saying that even while badly wounded, Machchhar managed to open the cockpit door and call for help.Read more: PM Modi heaps praise on flydubai pilot Captain Machchhar Captain Smit Machchhar, a Mumbaikar from Ghatkopar, is a commercial pilot who trained in New Zealand for his commercial pilot licence and later completed his Boeing 737 type rating at FSTC in Manesar, Gurgaon. He worked with SpiceJet for about a decade before joining flydubai in 2022.Machchhar, who is in his mid-30s, comes from a family with aviation ties, with his brother also working as a flydubai pilot. Friends and former colleagues describe him as a calm, decent and hardworking professional who was always willing to learn. He is currently recovering after being injured in the cockpit attack.Read more: How Indian pilot Smit Machchhar stopped Omani co-pilot from crashing plane
Article Summary: Captain Smit Machchhar was stabbed by his Omani co-pilot while fighting him in the cockpit, but fought back and was severely injured. The plane made an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia with all the passengers safe. Gujarat CM Bhupendra Patel: "This valiant son of Gujarat has illuminated the name of Gujarat and the nation across the globe"

Article Title: Chita Andolan is back: Why are Madhya Pradesh's Panna villagers protesting against Ken-Betwa project
Article Text:
MP dam project: Protesters brave rain and waterlogging for 20th day

What is happening in Madhya Pradesh's Panna?

Several women and other protesters had fallen ill after staying in water and rain for several days, with some suffering from wounds on their feet and other skin-related problems. (ANI photo)

So why are the protesters back?

For thousands of tribal families living in the path of the project, it has become a battle over land, forests, livelihoods and identity.

Affected families have staged some of the country's most striking demonstrations, standing waist-deep in river water, laying beside symbolic funeral pyres and even climbed symbolic gallows.

'Ken-Betwa River Linking Project' is India's first river-linking initiative aimed to transform the drought-prone Bundelkhand region through irrigation, drinking water supply and power generation.

What is the project aiming to accomplish?

Remember the unnerving visuals from Chita Andolan in Madhya Pradesh? Displaced Tribals sleeping on pyres, standing in water for their compensation. The unique protest is back and in its 20th day with agitators battling rain, waterlogging, lathicharge and general apathy by the authorities.Activist Amit Bhatnagar, Jai Kisan Sangathan leader, who has been on a hunger strike for the past four days, was arrested on Wednesday as protesters demonstrated chita, jal, sooli, mitti, bhook (pyre, water, gallows, soil, hunger) other forms of satyagraha.Bhatnagar accused the Panna administration of suppressing the agitation by lathicharging protesters, including women.Speaking to TOI before his arrest, Bhatnagar said, "For the past three days, the police have been bringing along people dressed in plain clothes, who misbehaved with women, entered their homes and even took away people’s phones which have still not been returned. When we approach the police, they ask who took the phones. How are people supposed to identify every face and find out who took them?""There is an atmosphere of fear in the villages. If we say anything, they start resorting to lathi-charge and filing false cases against the protesters," he added.“I am courting arrest because democracy is being murdered. Are we not even allowed to protest peacefully? We are putting ourselves through hardship to raise our concerns, but instead of listening to us, they have cut off the electricity and water. Even the British never did this. ”The latest protest follows a 15-day agitation in July, led largely by tribal women, after which the administration had assured protesters that eligible and genuinely displaced families would be transparently included in compensation and rehabilitation lists.However, the protesters claimed that they did not get the promised compensation. Also, their houses were now inundated, with two to three feet of water entering homes in several villages which now stand waterlogged including Mandalia, Tapariya and Kuwarpur."The families whose houses have been submerged are so poor that they have been forced to continue living there, or put up one makeshift shelter next to another, and then another. Earlier, the water would rise by half a foot at a time. But this time there was heavy rain on the 26th and 27th of September, followed by a 24-hour red alert, leaving them with no time to move. The villages turned into islands,” said Bhatnagar.The protesters claim that the compensation process remains incomplete, with several families receiving only Rs 5 lakh despite the government announcing a Rs 12.5-lakh package.They are also opposing the compensation conditions, which makes several tribals ineligible for relief.“The cut-off date under Section 11 has been set as 2018, which means people who are now 25-26 years old have received nothing. Those who are older are getting only Rs 5 lakh. What are families with eight or 10 children supposed to do?" asked Bhatnagar, adding that they were not against development projects, but that this development should not come at the cost of the rights of tribals.Bhatnagar pointed to Section 38 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013, which he said raised concerns about any displacement or submergence taking place before compensation and rehabilitation obligations had been fulfilled.“Villages and homes are now submerged. Houses have started collapsing and water has entered them. Yet, Section 38 of the 2013 law says that compensation for an irrigation project should be paid six months before submergence. If the houses were submerged two months ago, compensation should have been paid eight months earlier,” he said.The authorities, on the other hand, claim that they have been conducting fresh surveys and distributing compensation to affected families. TOI reached out to Chhatarpur district magistrate and is still awaiting a response from the administration.The Majhgawan dam project aims to transfer surplus water from Ken river to Betwa through the Daudhan Dam, a network of tunnels and a 221-km canal. It is supposed to address water shortages in drought-prone Bundelkhand region that spans across Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh.The project traces back to a plan introduced in 1980 and cleared in 2021 to connect the rivers. Prime Minister Narendra Modi laid its foundation stone in December 2024.The project is expected to improve agricultural output, curb migration and strengthen groundwater recharge through the revival of traditional Chandela-era ponds.
Article Summary: Tribal families living in the path of the project have staged some of the country's most striking demonstrations. The protest is back and in its 20th day with agitators battling rain, waterlogging, lathicharge and general apathy by the authorities.

Article Title: ‘Many are in contact’: Akhilesh claims BJP alliance MLAs in touch with SP ahead of Rajya Sabha polls
Article Text:
File photo: Samajwadi Party National President Akhilesh Yadav (Picture credit: PTI)

SP sticks to alliance, winnability formula

Rajya Sabha contest heats up

Yadav defends Nathwani candidature

Sugarcane payments and Raebareli remarks

NEW DELHI: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav on Wednesday claimed that several MLAs from the ruling BJP-led alliance in Uttar Pradesh are in contact with his party ahead of the Rajya Sabha elections, while saying the SP would not make commitments it could not honour.“There are many who are in contact. But how do we adjust them? We do not want to make a promise and then go back on it,” Yadav said at a press conference at the SP office.The remarks came as the SP formally entered the Rajya Sabha contest in Uttar Pradesh, with party candidates Professor Ram Gopal Yadav and Dhanraj Parimal Nathwani filing their nomination papers. Akhilesh Yadav accompanied both candidates during the filing.Asked about the party's plans for next year's Uttar Pradesh Assembly polls, Yadav said the alliance that existed earlier would continue. On seat-sharing, he reiterated that the SP would use winnability as the basis for deciding which party contests a seat.“The SP has said this earlier and I am saying it again -- winnability is the basis for a seat,” he said.The Election Commission has announced that polling for 11 Rajya Sabha seats, 10 from Uttar Pradesh and one from Uttarakhand, will be held on October 16.The terms of the sitting members from the two states are due to expire on November 25.Yadav said the democratic system requires representatives to be elected by the people and lawmakers to subsequently elect members of the Upper House.“Democracy should not have dishonesty. Had the BJP not indulged in dishonesty, the SP would have had three Rajya Sabha MPs,” he said, referring to the previous Rajya Sabha election in which SP candidate Alok Ranjan lost after cross-voting.Yadav said the SP was now urging MLAs to use the opportunity to “wash away the past”.Uttar Pradesh deputy chief minister Keshav Prasad Maurya , however, claimed that 25 SP MLAs were in touch with the BJP.“We will surprise them. 25 of their MLAs are in touch with us,” Maurya said, according to news agency ANI.His remarks came after the SP announced Ram Gopal Yadav and Nathwani as its two candidates.Uttar Pradesh minister and Suheldev Bharatiya Samaj Party chief Om Prakash Rajbhar also questioned whether the SP's candidates reflected its PDA — Pichhada, Dalit and Alpashankhyak — formulation.He cautioned the party against attempting to secure a third seat at the risk of losing its second.Defending the nomination of industrialist Dhanraj Parimal Nathwani, Yadav said he was pleased that the SP had the opportunity to send a representative of the younger generation and a “new way of thinking” to the Rajya Sabha.“The SP has decided to connect with the industrial sector and therefore, to make someone associated with the industry its Rajya Sabha member,” he said.Responding to criticism over backing an industrialist, Yadav said, “I think you should read about socialism again. I will give you a book by (Ram Manohar) Lohia.”He said socialist thought also focused on prosperity and equality and argued that governments across the country seek investment to drive economic growth.Yadav said the SP wanted to promote industries and employment in Uttar Pradesh, adding that the party would support those who contribute to economic growth, farmer employment and jobs for young people.Yadav also promised that sugarcane growers would receive pending payments within 24 to 48 hours if the SP formed the government in Uttar Pradesh. He said the party's election manifesto would include several measures for farmers.On his recent visit to Raebareli and allegations of police misconduct involving SP MLA Rahul Lodhi, Yadav questioned how police could behave in such a manner with an elected representative.“How can police behave like this with an elected representative?” he asked.He also said, “This time, it will be Lodhi versus (Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister) Yogi (Adityanath).”Yadav further said Uttar Pradesh's proposed target of becoming a USD 1-trillion economy could not be achieved through corruption, saying, “A USD-1-trillion economy will not be built through theft of offerings.”He also said the SP would continue to focus on farmers, recalling former prime minister Chaudhary Charan Singh and farmer leader Mahendra Singh Tikait.
Article Summary: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav claims several MLAs from ruling BJP-led alliance in Uttar Pradesh are in contact with his party. Yadav says the SP would not make commitments it could not honour. Election Commission has announced that polling for 11 Rajya Sabha seats, 10 from Uttar Pradesh and one from Uttarakhand, will be held on October 16.

Article Title: Flydubai flight drama: How Indian pilot Smit Machchhar stopped Omani co-pilot from crashing plane
Article Text:
The captain has years of experience and was a SpiceJet pilot till 2022

What happened inside the cockpit

Flydubai confirms incident

NEW DELHI: An Indian pilot has been identified as the captain who helped prevent a flydubai passenger plane from crashing after his co-pilot allegedly tried to take control of the aircraft during a flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv, according to Israeli media reports and an Israeli journalist.The Indian pilot has been identified as Captain Smit Machchhar, based in Dubai, who intervened to stop his Omani co-pilot allegedly trying to take control of the aircraft and crash it.The Indian captain was stabbed repeatedly and drenched in blood, according to various witness reports and officials.Machchhar is an experienced commercial pilot with more than 13 years of flying experience on Boeing 737 aircraft. He has been a captain with flydubai since June 2022, having previously spent 11 years with SpiceJet, where he served as a senior commander and Line Training Captain.During his time at SpiceJet, Machchhar reportedly flew more than 9,500 hours, including over 6,400 hours as pilot-in-command, and served as a Line Training Captain from November 2020 to June 2022. His experience includes pilot training and mentoring, crew resource management, flight standards and compliance, and B737 NG and MAX operations.The incident unfolded aboard flydubai Flight FZ1073 on Wednesday, with the Boeing 737 sending emergency signals before making an emergency landing in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia. The flight was carrying around 180 Israeli passengers, all of whom were reported safe.Also read: Passengers recall harrowing ordeal on flight that nearly crashed The flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv was flying over Jordan when it transmitted an emergency signal, followed by another signal indicating possible unlawful interference.Israeli officials said the emergency signals followed a physical altercation between the two pilots. Reuters reported that the co-pilot was believed to have stabbed the captain before cabin crew entered the cockpit. Both pilots were later hospitalised after the aircraft landed in Tabuk.Israeli media reports said the suspected attacker attempted to take control of the aircraft and force it into a descent. Passengers reportedly heard screaming and saw blood inside the cockpit.Flight-tracking data showed the aircraft plunging rapidly from around 34,000 feet to about 20,000 feet, with Reuters reporting a drop of nearly 14,000 feet in less than 30 seconds before the aircraft stabilised.The aircraft was initially treated as a possible hijacking, prompting Israeli fighter jets to be scrambled. The Israeli prime minister's office later said the incident was not believed to have been a hijacking.Israeli media reports have described the incident as a possible attempted suicide or deliberate crash, while Israeli officials cited by Reuters said they were assessing it as a possible attempted "terror attack". Reuters also reported that officials did not believe the incident was related to a mental-health issue.Later, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said the pilots became involved in a physical altercation as the flight approached Israel. “During the flight as they approached the country one of the pilots stabbed the other pilot,” Netanyahu said in a video address.“Apparently he tried to crash the plane with its occupants.” Netanyahu added “almost all” passengers were Israelis, with some passengers and crew members breaking into the cockpit and subduing the attacker. “I spoke with one of the Israeli passengers. He told me that the plane went into a spin and began to dive. He told me that somehow he managed to break into the cockpit with one of the crew members and together they neutralized the stabbing pilot while he was trying to sabotage the aircraft’s systems,” Netanyahu said. “Another air crew that was on the plane entered the cockpit and managed to stabilize the plane,” he added. He also praised those who intervened, saying: “I salute these heroes who showed exceptional resourcefulness and courage.They saved many lives and prevented a major disaster.”Also read: Israel security minister on flydubai cockpit incident Flydubai has confirmed that Flight FZ1073 experienced an incident during its journey from Dubai to Tel Aviv and diverted to Tabuk, where it landed safely."Our teams are working closely with the relevant authorities. Further updates will be issued as additional confirmed details become available," the airline said.Read more: Passenger's mother says pilot tried to kill co-pilot on Flydubai flight The airline has not publicly confirmed the identities or nationalities of the pilots or provided details about what happened inside the cockpit.The investigation is continuing, with Israeli authorities examining the circumstances of the cockpit confrontation, the alleged attempt to take control of the aircraft and the security clearance given to the crew.
Article Summary: Indian pilot identified as Captain Smit Machchhar, based in Dubai. He intervened to stop his Omani co-pilot allegedly trying to take control of the aircraft and crash it. The Indian captain was stabbed repeatedly and drenched in blood, according to various witness reports and officials.

Attacked by his Omani national co-pilot, the captain, who hails from Ghatkopar and is learnt to be in mid 30s, he managed to both fight off the assailant and regain control of the aircraft despite being injured.Displaying a crucial presence of mind in most sudden and severe circumstances, he managed to save the plane from plunging — something the Boeing 737 MAX was very close to at that point of time. According to tracking site Flightradar24, the plane (A6-FKF) operating as FZ 1073 had dropped over 14,000 feet (about 4.3 km) from 30,875 feet to 16,750 feet in just 29 seconds. “Flightradar24 data recorded an extreme descent rate of approximately 30,000 feet per minute.Also read: Flydubai flight drama: How Indian pilot Smit Machchhar stopped Omani co-pilot from crashing planeE For this flight which had 174 passengers of whom 166 were Israeli citizens, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said in a video address: “During the flight as they approached the country one of the pilots stabbed the other pilot. Apparently he tried to crash the plane with its occupants.”Captain Smit Machchhar managed to save the aircraft from a fatal plunge at this crucial time.Just as he stabilised the aircraft, crew members opened the cockpit door and managed to overpower the assailant co-pilot. FZ 1073 had two more pilots travelling as passengers who were to operate the aircraft back to Dubai from Tel Aviv. Once the situation in the flight deck was controlled, these two pilots took over the aircraft and safely diverted it to Saudi Arabia’s Tabuk with its rudder — used for directional control — getting detached during the sharp plunge.A flydubai spokesperson confirmed that “an altercation occurred” in the flight deck.Captain Machchhar, who worked in SpiceJet for about a decade till 2023, is learnt to be stable. Multiple friends and colleagues remember him as a “great guy” and are praying for his recovery. “He did his commercial pilot licence (CPL) training from New Zealand and then his type rating on the Boeing 737 at FSTC in Manesar (Gurgaon). He is a very decent and sober person ever willing to learn. There is not a single negative thing that I can recall about him,” said a senior pilot who trained him. Smit’s brother is also a pilot who flies for flydubai.
Article Summary: Captain Smit Machchhar, who hails from Ghatkopar and is learnt to be in mid 30s, managed to both fight off the assailant and regain control of the aircraft. Despite being severely injured, he managed to unlock the cockpit door - allowing Israeli passengers and Emirati crew to intervene and save all the passengers.

Article Title: 'A true hero': Netanyahu 'salutes' Indian pilot who stopped Omani co-pilot from crashing Flydubai plane

Indian pilot stable in Saudi hospital

NEW DELHI: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Wednesday praised Indian flydubai pilot Captain Smit Machchhar for his bravery after he was seriously injured in a cockpit altercation that forced a Dubai-Tel Aviv flight to make an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia. Netanyahu met passengers after they returned to Israel and said the actions of Machchhar, passengers and crew had helped avert a major disaster.“My salute to the Indian pilot Captain Smit Machchhar for his extraordinary bravery. Despite being stabbed and seriously injured, he fought back, resisted, opened the cockpit door, and enabled passengers and crew to overpower the attacker — preventing a catastrophic mid-air disaster,” Netanyahu said in a post.“He saved the lives of 174 people, including Israeli citizens and other nationals. I wish Captain Machchhar a speedy and full recovery. He is a true hero,” he said.The Indian Embassy in Riyadh said Machchhar was receiving treatment at a hospital in Tabuk and was in stable condition.“Our Embassy in Riyadh and Consulate in Jeddah have been following the health condition of Mr Smit Machchhar, the brave Indian pilot of Flydubai flight that was diverted to Tabuk today,” it said in a post on X.“A full update on his health is awaited but he is reported to be in stable condition,” the embassy said, adding that it was in contact with his family and Saudi authorities.The embassy said it would continue to follow up on his health and provide all possible assistance for his wellbeing.Netanyahu met passengers after a rescue flight carrying around 180 people, most of them Israelis, landed at Ben Gurion International Airport.Describing the episode as an “extremely serious security incident”, Netanyahu praised the passengers and crew members who intervened during the flight. He said they had shown “exceptional resourcefulness and courage” and “saved many lives” by preventing what he described as a major disaster.Netanyahu also said the pilot accused of attacking the other pilot had been arrested and was being interrogated by Saudi authorities.Israeli passenger Yaniv, who was among those who intervened, later told Netanyahu that he entered the cockpit and found the alleged attacker at the aircraft's controls.“When I went in, I saw the terrorist on the controls, between the two seats. There were no pilots in the seats,” Yaniv said, according to The Times of Israel.He said he pulled the man away from the controls and called on other passengers to restrain him. When he realised the aircraft was tilting sharply, Yaniv said he returned to the cockpit and pulled back on the controls until the aircraft began to level out.He said he knew what to do because “I watch Mayday”, referring to the aviation accident documentary series.“The plane started leveling out a little more, and then the pilot told me he was taking over from there,” he said.Another passenger, Tzika Manes, told Israel's Channel 12 that he and two other Israeli passengers helped subdue the alleged attacker.Manes said his wife had heard screams and sounds of a struggle near the cockpit and alerted a flight attendant. He said passengers were thrown around the cabin as the aircraft lost altitude.The three passengers eventually restrained the alleged attacker using corded headphones, with the effort taking around 20 to 25 minutes, according to Manes.A doctor travelling on the flight also helped treat the injured pilot, he said.The flydubai flight was diverted to Tabuk in north-western Saudi Arabia and made an emergency landing there.The passengers were subsequently flown back to Israel on a rescue flight. The Israel Airports Authority had earlier set up a dedicated waiting and information area at Ben Gurion Airport for relatives of those on board.Netanyahu's office said the situation had been brought under control and that Israeli authorities were working to ensure the passengers' safe return.Israel scrambled fighter jets after concerns that the aircraft could have been hijacked, according to reports citing Israeli officials.The incident prompted security consultations in Israel, while authorities maintained contact with Saudi officials over the passengers and the investigation.An Israeli official described the episode as a “severe disaster” that had been averted.Flydubai confirmed that flight FZ1073, travelling from Dubai International Airport to Ben Gurion Airport, had experienced an incident and landed safely in Tabuk.“Our teams are working closely with the relevant authorities,” the airline said.The airline did not provide details of the cockpit altercation.The incident involved an altercation between the pilots while the aircraft was travelling from Dubai to Tel Aviv.An Israeli official told AP that one of the pilots was armed with a knife. Reuters reported that the co-pilot was believed to have stabbed the captain before cabin crew entered the cockpit.The captain and first officer were injured and taken to hospital, according to Tabuk airport authorities cited by Saudi state television.Netanyahu said the evidence indicated that one pilot had stabbed the other and apparently attempted to crash the aircraft.Publicly available flight-tracking data showed that the aircraft transmitted an emergency alert around two-and-a-half hours after departing Dubai and subsequently dropped sharply from about 33,000 feet to 17,000 feet within roughly a minute before making an erratic turn near the Jordanian border.The circumstances of the cockpit altercation remain under investigation.Saudi authorities are questioning the alleged attacker, while Israeli authorities are examining the security implications of the incident and are expected to question passengers after their return.Transport minister Miri Regev asked Israel's Civil Aviation Authority to investigate what she described as an alleged violation of the aviation agreement between Israel and the UAE. She also called for flydubai flights to Israel to be suspended.Israeli media reported that Machchhar was of Indian origin and that the other pilot was reportedly Omani. Those nationality details had not been independently confirmed by flydubai.Reports also said a second team of pilots in civilian clothes was aboard the aircraft and helped prevent one of the pilots from taking control, though that detail had not been independently confirmed.The investigation remains underway, with flydubai saying it is working with the relevant authorities.
Article Summary: Captain Smit Machchhar, an Indian national based in Dubai, was reportedly stabbed and severely wounded during the incident. According to Israeli reports, he intervened after an alleged attempt to crash the aircraft. Israel scrambled fighter jets after concerns that the aircraft could have been hijacked, according to reports.

Article Title: What makes a rape case 'rarest of rare'? How courts decide on the death penalty
Article Text:
Should death penalty remain exception in rape cases, not the rule?

And should death remain an exception rather than the rule?

Why women's safety is back at the centre of debate

2026 witness​es shocking incidents of sexual assault

When does rape become 'rarest of rare'?

Activist Yogita Bhayana in conversation with TOI

What changes when the accused is a minor?

Minor victims in rape cases in India: NCRB data

Does a harsher sentence always mean justice?

Two cases with different court sentences

Why tougher laws alone may not be enough

Delhi University students take out protest march amid rains to Miranda House college in north campus over women safety after Kalkaji gang rape.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Every time a brutal rape case shocks the country, the demand returns almost immediately: give the harshest possible punishment.The anger is understandable. But the law applies a much narrower test. Not every rape case, however grave, crosses the threshold for the death penalty.India recorded 29,536 rape cases in 2024, according to the latest National Crime Records Bureau data. In Delhi, 1,058 rape cases were registered that year, while Delhi Police reported 1,901 cases in 2025.The figures come amid renewed attention on sexual violence, with a series of recent cases in Delhi and across the country bringing questions of punishment, deterrence and justice back into focus.While Indian law provides for stringent punishment, including the death penalty in certain rape cases, capital punishment remains restricted to specific circumstances.So when does a rape case cross the legal threshold for the ultimate punishment? What makes one case “rarest of rare”, while another results in life imprisonment?A series of recent cases has once again put women’s safety under scrutiny.In September, a 17-year-old girl was allegedly gang-raped by three men posing as police personnel at Astha Kunj Park near Kalkaji Mandir in Delhi. The case triggered student protests demanding stronger measures for women’s safety, and police arrested the accused.In August, another 17-year-old girl was allegedly gang-raped by a bus driver and conductor after boarding a bus from Greater Noida. She was later dropped near Kashmere Gate. The National Human Rights Commission took suo motu cognisance of the case and sought reports from authorities.Against this backdrop, the Supreme Court on Monday took suo motu cognisance of recent rape incidents in Delhi-NCR, flagging what it described as a "systematic failure" to ensure basic public safety.Concerns have extended beyond Delhi.In Bihar, three incidents involving alleged sexual harassment and assault were reported within days. In Jamui, a teenage boy and girl were allegedly stopped and assaulted by a group of men on September 19, with three accused arrested after a video surfaced online. In Samastipur, a minor girl was allegedly assaulted and molested, while another case in Banka’s Mandar Hill area involved allegations of a woman being harassed and her male friend assaulted.The cases have also spilled onto the streets. Students and young people in the national capital are holding protests demanding safer public spaces, stronger policing and greater accountability.Indian law permits the death penalty in certain aggravated rape cases, including those involving minors and cases where the victim dies or is left in a persistent vegetative state, under provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and the POCSO Act.But the existence of the death penalty does not mean it follows automatically in the most brutal cases.Advocate Sumit Nagpal said courts consider factors including the brutality of the offence, injuries caused, the vulnerability of the survivor and the long-term consequences while determining punishment.Rupali Jain, who practises in the high court and Supreme Court, said the harm caused by rape, while grave, cannot by itself justify capital punishment."As harm is inherent in every rape, it cannot alone justify death. The court must also apply the 'criminal test', the offender’s age, antecedents, background, custodial conduct and prospects of reform, as reiterated in Manoj v. State of Madhya Pradesh (2022)," she said.The "rarest of rare" doctrine gained renewed attention following the 2012 Nirbhaya case . On December 16, 2012, a 23-year-old woman was gang-raped and brutally assaulted inside a moving bus in Delhi. She died from her injuries days later.Four adult accused were sentenced to death by the trial court in 2013. The Delhi high court upheld the punishment in 2014, and the Supreme Court confirmed the death sentences in 2017, holding that the case fell within the “rarest of rare” category.However, the Supreme Court has also held that the brutality or heinousness of an offence alone does not automatically make it a "rarest of rare" case. Courts must weigh aggravating circumstances against mitigating factors, including the possibility of reform and rehabilitation.But the death penalty is not automatic, even in cases involving extreme violence.The Bilkis Bano case offers another example of how courts apply the 'rarest of rare' test differently.In the Bilkis Bano case, 11 men were convicted and sentenced to life imprisonment for gang rape, murder and other offences linked to the 2002 Gujarat riots. Bilkis was 21 and five months pregnant when she was raped, and several members of her family were killed.The case shows why the "rarest of rare" test is not based only on how brutal or shocking a crime appears. Courts must also consider other factors, including the background of the accused and whether there is any possibility of reform.Activist Yogita Bhayana, however, argues that the impact of rape on the survivor should receive greater weight when courts consider the threshold."Every rape case is rarest of the rare in terms of the victim," she said, arguing that the legal system can focus heavily on physical brutality while overlooking the lasting impact on survivors.Bhayana said she believes the death penalty should remain available in rape cases and argued for greater weight to be given to the consequences of the crime for survivors while deciding punishment.Jain, too, stressed the need for severe punishment, while emphasising that its deterrent effect depends on certainty and speed of enforcement."In my opinion, the most effective way to deter sexual violence is stern punishment, imposed swiftly and with certainty. The offender must know that the consequence is severe and unavoidable: imprisonment for the remainder of natural life and, in the rarest of cases, death. The statute already provides for this, as Sections 65, 66, 70 and 71 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 prescribe natural-life imprisonment or death for the gravest forms. The deficit lies in enforcement."The legal process changes significantly when the accused is under 18.Under the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015, a child aged between 16 and 18 who is accused of a “heinous offence”, including rape, can undergo a preliminary assessment by the Juvenile Justice Board.The Board looks at the child’s mental and physical capacity to commit the offence, whether they understood its consequences and the circumstances in which the alleged offence took place.Depending on that assessment, the case can be transferred to the Children’s Court, which then decides whether the child should be tried as an adult.Rupali Jain said the existing law already provides a framework for dealing with serious offences committed by juveniles, and the focus should remain on how it is implemented rather than simply lowering the age threshold.She also pointed out that the Juvenile Justice Act bars the death penalty and life imprisonment without the possibility of release for a child in conflict with law.However, activist Yogita Bhayana argues that the distinction between different degrees of brutality can be deeply troubling for survivors.“The miner will be treated as miner unless he brutally kills her, rape her in a very gruesome manner. Then otherwise, it will not be in the rarest of the rare category. So we need to change the whole thing,” she said, arguing that the system should focus more closely on the impact of the crime on the survivor and called for greater awareness and stronger mechanisms to deal with sexual offences.For survivors, justice does not necessarily end with an arrest, conviction or sentence.Activist Yogita Bhayana said the distinction between "high-profile" and ordinary rape cases often comes from media attention rather than the nature of the crime or the survivor’s experience."There is no case which is high profile. What becomes media-highlighted becomes high profile," she said, pointing out that even Nirbhaya came from a humble, lower-middle-class family.She said survivors often continue to deal with trauma, repeated questioning and the pressures of the legal process long after public attention has moved on."Attention doesn’t mean justice," Bhayana said.Dr Vinodh Sreeram, senior psychiatrist & addiction specialist at Maarga Mind Care, Bengaluru, said rape can deeply alter a survivor’s sense of safety, relationships and ability to return to everyday life.He cautioned against judging trauma only by visible injuries or by how brutal an assault appears. Two survivors of similar incidents can experience very different psychological effects depending on factors such as age, past experiences, their relationship with the accused and the support available to them."The absence of visible injury should never be mistaken for the absence of psychological trauma," he said.On whether the death penalty can provide psychological closure, Sreeram said there is no single answer. Some survivors or families may see a severe sentence as justice, but "closure rarely comes from the sentence alone".Being believed, treated with dignity, protected from further harm and supported through recovery can be just as important, he said. Repeated questioning, cross-examination, delays and prolonged appeals can themselves become additional sources of distress.Recent protests in Delhi have again brought demands for safer public spaces, stronger policing, better surveillance and greater accountability to the forefront.Advocate Sumit Nagpal said the biggest challenge is not necessarily the absence of laws, but the capacity to enforce them."The bottleneck is capacity, not the statute. India has roughly twenty judges per million people against a recommended fifty, and police strength sits well below sanctioned levels in most states. Until that gap closes, every reform stays on paper," he said."So the real agenda is unglamorous: more investigators, more courts, more forensic capacity, fewer vacancies. No amendment will substitute for that."Activist Yogita Bhayana said the biggest gap remains implementation. While reforms, awareness and gender-sensitisation efforts have increased, she said survivors continue to face inadequate support, delays in fast-track courts and a lack of sensitivity within the system.She also warned that repeated exposure to sexual-violence cases can make institutions become "immune" to such crimes."For them, they see it like an everyday thing," she said, arguing that continued training and sensitisation are needed to ensure sexual violence is not treated as routine.Dr Vinodh Sreeram said debates around harsher punishment must also account for the realities of reporting, particularly because many survivors know the accused and may face fear, stigma and family pressure.A trauma-informed justice system, he said, should focus on sensitive questioning, privacy, timely trials and access to psychological support.“Justice is not only about the severity of punishment. It is also about ensuring that survivors are heard, protected, treated with dignity and given the opportunity to rebuild their lives,” Sreeram said.The death penalty is only one part of the debate. The larger challenge is to prevent such crimes, ensure quicker justice and make sure survivors get the support they need.
Article Summary: India recorded 29,536 rape cases in 2024, according to the latest National Crime Records Bureau data. In Delhi, 1,058 rape cases were registered that year, while Delhi Police reported 1,901 cases in 2025. Figures come amid renewed attention on sexual violence, with a series of recent cases in Delhi and across the country.

NEW DELHI: A special National Investigation Agency (NIA) court has directed that charges be framed against separatist Yasin Malik and six other accused under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) for allegedly receiving foreign funding from the Pakistani establishment through hawala channels.The other accused are Zahoor Ahmed Shah Watali, Abdul Rashid Sheikh, Shabir Ahmad Shah, Naval Kishore Kapoor, Trison Farms and Construction Pvt Ltd, and Masarat Alam Bhat.Special NIA Judge Prashant Sharma ordered that charges be framed after considering the material against the accused."I conclude that prima facie, there is sufficient material on record based upon which strong suspicion is raised against all seven accused persons, namely Zahoor Ahmad Shah Watali, Naval Kishore Kapoor, M/s Trison Farms and Constructions Pvt Ltd, Mohd. SRINAGAR/ NEW DELHI: In a joint operation by Army, police and security forces, a top Pakistani Lashkar-e-Taiba terrorist, identified as Mohammad Asif, alias Hashim Musa, was killed in an overnight encounter in the upper reaches of Yousmarg, around 60km from Srinagar.With his elimination, the entire group of four LeT commanders who had been operating in J&K since 2022 and were also behind the Pahalgam massacre has been wiped out. They were linked to the Oct 2024 Gagangir attack in Ganderbal, which claimed the lives of seven, and the Bootapathri attack near Gulmarg that killed two soldiers and two civilians. The violent spree culminated in the devastating April 2025 Baisaran Valley attack in Pahalgam, where the terrorists massacred 26 tourists and a local horseman.
Article Summary: A top Pakistani Lashkar-e-Taiba terrorist, identified as Mohammad Asif, alias Hashim Musa, was killed in an overnight encounter in the upper reaches of Yousmarg. Intelligence agencies had been tracking for two years the whereabouts of this former Pak Special Service Group (SSG) commando who had infiltrated into the Valley.

Article Title: Modi and Trump discuss ties, PM flags concerns about US’ Russia law

PM Narendra Modi held a phone call with US President Donald Trump Wednesday to review bilateral cooperation in trade, defence, critical technologies and energy, amid increasing friction in the relationship driven primarily by India’s purchase of Russian oil.Modi is learnt to have touched upon India’s concerns related to the US’ latest Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 (SRIA) that allows the president to impose up to 100 percent tariffs on countries like India and China for their procurement of Russian oil.In the run up to the Modi-Trump conversation – their first since they met in France in June – both external affairs minister S Jaishankar and foreign secretary Vikram Misri had flagged the same concerns with American authorities, emphasising the recently enacted SRIA would have consequences for India-US ties. India continues to maintain that its energy sourcing is driven by national interests and the need to ensure reliable and affordable supplies for 1.4 billion people.Modi said in a post on X that he had productive conversation with Trump. “We reviewed our bilateral cooperation in trade, defence, energy, critical technologies and other areas. We agreed to maintain close engagement to take our Comprehensive Global Strategic Partnership forward,” said the PM, adding that they also exchanged views on regional and international issues, including ongoing efforts to advance global peace and security.An Indian readout said they agreed to maintain close engagement to deepen cooperation for the benefit of the people of both countries, and also to remain in touch. There was no White House readout till late in the evening.According to diplomatic sources, the conversation helped reinforce the strategic partnership amid the friction over the US passage of the Russia-related legislation, and also differences over trade that have prevented the 2 countries from concluding a bilateral trade agreement. Modi will travel to the US in December for the G20 summit in Florida where he is likely to also have a bilateral meeting with Trump. However, potential US tariffs or penalties could disrupt the diplomatic buildup to the visit.Jaishankar had raised India’s concerns related to the SRIA with his counterpart Marco Rubio in a meeting on the margins of the UNGA last week. Earlier this week, foreign secretary Vikram Misri told a visiting Congressional delegation that the new law will have a negative impact on not just bilateral relations but also the energy situation in global markets.Trade and energy, however, are not the only issues that India and the US need to address to get the relationship back on track. While still in the US, Jaishankar warned the Trump administration this week that the lack of empathy or understanding about India’s cross-border terrorism concerns – as evident from the US courting of Pakistan – will also hurt the relationship.

SRINAGAR: Two top officials of the J&K administration came under fire Wednesday from political parties in the union territory for writing to the Assembly and asking it not to proceed with the resolution for the restoration of statehood, which also contained a reference to autonomy and was passed by the House on Monday.Peoples Conference, PDP and Congress sought action against chief secretary Atal Dulloo and the law secretary.Speaking on Wednesday, the last day of the Assembly’s autumn session, Peoples Conference chairman Sajad Lone said the two officials had undermined the House and sought action against them. “The act of the chief secretary of writing a letter to the Assembly is a disdainful act of brutality against the Assembly. NEW DELHI: The killing of senior Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) commander Mohammad Asif alias Hashim Musa in Jammu and Kashmir's Budgam district on Wednesday was the culmination of a months-long intelligence-led operation, named ‘Operation Sheruwali’, launched in May 2026.Security forces had been tracking Musa for a prolonged period before a coordinated plan involving multiple agencies was drawn up to neutralise him, following the receipt of technical and human intelligence about his movements and presence in the area.The operation culminated in an encounter in the Yousmarg area of Budgam, where Musa was killed. His body was later recovered along with war-like stores, according to the Army.Also read| Ex-Pakistan SSG commando, highly trained LeT terrorist, Pahalgam mastermind: Who was Hashim Moosa; killed in J&K encounter The ministry of information and broadcasting said the operation dealt a blow to the LeT network in Jammu and Kashmir, with Musa's killing bringing an end to a group of four senior commanders who had been operating in the union territory since 2022 and were linked to several attacks.According to a statement issued by the Press Information Bureau (PIB), security forces had been pursuing Musa for a long time.A specific plan involving all stakeholders was recently put in place after intelligence inputs indicated his movement and presence.The government said the operation to neutralise Musa was part of the ongoing ‘Operation Sheruwali’, which began in May 2026.The Army's Chinar Corps, meanwhile, said the encounter took place during Operation Korag in the Yousmarg area of Budgam district. Troops launched a search operation based on specific intelligence inputs and challenged suspicious movement, following which terrorists opened fire.The operation involved the Indian Army, Jammu and Kashmir Police and the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF).The search continued after the encounter, with security personnel checking the surrounding areas for any additional terrorist presence. Musa's body was recovered from the general area of Palmaidan along with war-like stores, according to the Chinar Corps.One of the key aspects of Musa's background is his alleged association with Pakistan's military.ANI, quoting security agency sources, reported that Musa had served as a para-commando in Pakistan's Special Service Group (SSG), where he held the rank of Havildar. According to the sources, he retired from the SSG in 2023, subsequently joined the LeT and infiltrated into India.Former Jammu and Kashmir DGP S P Vaid described Musa as a highly trained commando specialising in ambushes and guerrilla-style attacks.Vaid alleged that Musa's footprints had been seen in several attacks in Jammu and Kashmir, including those in Poonch, DKG, Bhimber Gali, Gulmarg and the attack on pilgrims in Reasi.However, his alleged military background has been reported by security agency sources and has not been independently established.With Musa's killing, all four senior LeT commanders belonging to the group that had been active in Jammu and Kashmir since 2022 have been neutralised, according to the government.The government linked the group to several attacks across Jammu and Kashmir, including the Halan attack in August 2023, DKG attack in December 2023, Kandi attack in May 2023, Shahsitar attack in May 2024, Shiv Khori attack in June 2024, Gagangir and Bootapathri attacks in October 2024, and the Baisaran attack in April 2025.Musa was among the key suspects in the April 22, 2025, Pahalgam terror attack , in which terrorists targeted tourists at Baisaran Valley, killing 26 people.The Jammu and Kashmir Police had announced a reward of Rs 20 lakh for information leading to the arrest of Pakistan nationals and LeT terrorists Adil Hussain Thoker, Ali Bhai and Hashim Musa.The National Investigation Agency (NIA) subsequently chargesheeted seven accused in the case, including Pakistan-based LeT and The Resistance Front (TRF), which it accused of planning, facilitating and executing the attack.The NIA's 1,597-page chargesheet also named Pakistani handler Sajid Jatt as an accused and detailed the alleged Pakistan-based conspiracy behind the attack.The government said the operation reflected sustained coordination between the Jammu and Kashmir Police, the Indian Army and Central Armed Police Forces (CAPFs) in counter-terrorism operations across the union territory.
Article Summary: Hashim Moosa killed in an encounter in Jammu and Kashmir’s Budgam district, Indian Army says. Security forces had been tracking Musa for a prolonged period before a coordinated plan involving multiple agencies was drawn up to neutralise him. His body was later recovered along with war-like stores, according to the Army.

Article Title: 'This nonsense has to stop': SC pulls up UP Police over unnamed FIRs, suggests CBI probe in all cases
Article Text:
SC lambasts UP Police over unnamed FIR despite accused being known, suggests CBI take over all UP cases

SC seeks explanation from UP government

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Wednesday strongly criticised the Uttar Pradesh Police for allegedly registering an FIR against an unknown person despite knowing the identity of the accused, questioning how people could trust the police under such circumstances.A bench of Justices Sanjay Kumar and Sanjeev Sachdeva suggested that the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) take over all criminal investigations in Uttar Pradesh and even remarked that the entire state police force could be disbanded.“Why did you write unknown if the person was caught at the spot? How will people trust the police?” the court asked.The bench further said, "Toeing the line is one thing but bending over is another. And this kind of cover-up job? Less said the better."Directing the station house officer (SHO) to remain present in court on the next date of hearing, the bench questioned the police investigation and said, "This is how you do the investigation. We have seen lacunae in many cases. In everything, you have an agenda. How will people trust you if this is how you proceed with these matters?"It is better if we ask the CBI to step in and take over all UP Police investigations.We might as well disband the UP Police. This nonsense has to stop at some point."The observations came during the hearing of a woman's plea seeking cancellation of anticipatory bail granted to an accused in a case registered under Section 354 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC).The petitioner, who appeared in person, alleged that the police had initially registered an FIR against an "unknown person" despite her having handed the accused over to them after he allegedly trespassed into a private space and harassed her.She further alleged that the police added the accused's name to their report only after the court sought an explanation, without conducting any investigation, and described the police report as "biased".The bench also questioned the possibility of an accused's name being introduced later through supplementary documents.“Perhaps…. you can substitute the name, bring in one of your own names…” the court observed.The Supreme Court noted that the Uttar Pradesh Police's affidavit itself disclosed the accused's name, despite it allegedly being omitted from the FIR. The bench sought an explanation from the state administration over the circumstances in which the FIR was registered and directed it to file a fresh affidavit.The court further remarked that following instructions was one thing, but going to such lengths to protect or cover up the conduct in question was unacceptable.The woman had initially approached a lower court, which granted anticipatory bail to the accused. She subsequently moved the Allahabad High Court seeking cancellation of the bail, but her plea was rejected.She then approached the Supreme Court challenging the high court's order.During the hearing, the petitioner alleged that the accused's name was introduced into the case only after the High Court sought a report, and that he was eventually given a clean chit. The Supreme Court expressed shock at the submission.However, advocate Vijendra Singh, representing the Uttar Pradesh Police, denied that the court had made adverse observations against the state police.According to the advocate-on-record, the bench had only taken note of the petitioner's submissions and sought an affidavit from the UP Police. The Uttar Pradesh government said it would respond to the allegations before the court.
Article Summary: Supreme Court criticises Uttar Pradesh Police for allegedly registering an FIR against an unknown person despite knowing the identity of the accused. Justices Sanjay Kumar and Sanjeev Sachdeva suggested that the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) take over all criminal investigations in Uttar Pradesh.
